subject: general
question: Find the value of sqrt{125 + sqrt{344 + sqrt{289}}}.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **nested square roots** from the innermost part to the outermost.

√289 = 17

√(344 + 17) = √361 = 19

√(125 + 19) = √144 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sqrt{125 + sqrt{344 + sqrt{289}}}

**Step 1:** Evaluate the innermost square root.

⇒ √289 = 17 (since 17² = 289)

**Step 2:** Substitute this value back into the expression.

⇒ √(125 + √(344 + 17))

⇒ √(125 + √361)

**Step 3:** Evaluate the next square root.

⇒ √361 = 19 (since 19² = 361)

**Step 4:** Substitute this value and solve the final square root.

⇒ √(125 + 19)

⇒ √144

⇒ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares

Remembering **perfect squares** up to 30 is crucial for **simplification**. For example, 13²=169, 14²=196, 15²=225, etc.

BODMAS in Surds

Always simplify the **innermost bracket** or radical sign first before moving to the outer operations.

Unit Digit Trick

If a number ends in 9, its square root will end in either 3 or 7. For √289, since 10²=100 and 20²=400, the answer must be 13 or 17.</p
